headline: High risk of shared-filesystem prompt injection and write conflicts; default configs also enable cascading edits between two open-source coding agents.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write the user filesystem, and Agent A also uses MCP while Agent B consumes files passed on the command line. That creates a plausible shared-content bridge where attacker-controlled file content can be treated as instructions. This is not provably blocked by either profile, though it is not a direct shared channel by default.
conditions: IF either agent reads untrusted files from the shared workspace as instructions
IF Agent A exposes MCP content into files that Agent B later parses
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable MCP extensions for Agent A during paired runs
Require a human review step before either agent acts on file content
Prefix untrusted file content with explicit non-instruction markers
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch source code and files in the working directory, and both have broad network egress to configured model providers. Shared filesystem access means one agent can expose data the other can read, and either agent may upload that context to its backend. The profiles do not show a hard isolation boundary, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF sensitive files are present in the shared workspace
IF either agent forwards file contents into its model-provider context
mitigations: Use a dedicated workspace with only necessary files
Remove secrets before starting either agent
Restrict outbound network access for the session
Run one agent at a time on sensitive repositories
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent file allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have write_filesystem and modify_git_state, and both share state via the filesystem. That makes concurrent edits and git-state races likely without explicit locking. Because the same repo can be mutated by both, conflicts can corrupt work or overwrite changes in default paired use.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository concurrently
IF git operations occur without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Serialize edits so only one agent writes at a time
Use separate branches per agent
Add a manual merge checkpoint after each agent
Pause one agent while the other commits
requires-engineering: implement workspace locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent B produces diff-based edit proposals and can act on files from the workspace, while Agent A can generate tool-mediated outputs from MCP and shell-enabled workflows. If B treats A's output as authoritative, errors can cascade into incorrect edits or commits. The profiles do not prove direct automation, so medium is appropriate rather than high.
conditions: IF Agent B consumes Agent A's text output without verification
IF Agent A's generated content is copied into B's edit workflow
mitigations: Require B to cite source files before editing
Insert a human verification step between agents
Limit Agent A to drafting only, not final instructions
Compare diffs against original files before applying
requires-engineering: add structured handoff validation

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source coding agents with similar data classes and no explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch documented. The only compliance-relevant issue visible is that both handle source code and model-provider keys, but the profiles do not show a cross-border or regulated-data violation. The other agent is cited because the risk is pairwise workspace handling.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed in the shared workspace
IF either agent's provider retention policy differs from the repository's compliance requirements
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the shared workspace
Review provider retention settings before use
Use non-sensitive sample repositories
Document which agent may see which files
requires-engineering: add compliance policy enforcement
